title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic low back pain.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation of his chronic low back pain. He reports that the pain has been persistent for several months, primarily localized to the lumbar region. He describes the sensation as a dull ache that occasionally sharpens with prolonged standing or walking. He notes that the pain is most severe at the end of the day and does not typically radiate into his lower extremities. He has been utilizing heat therapy at home with moderate relief. He denies any recent falls, new-onset numbness, or weakness in his legs. He reports that his current activity level remains stable, though he finds it difficult to perform heavy lifting.

Review of Systems
The patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or recent weight changes. He denies any headaches, vision changes, or urinary incontinence. He reports no joint swelling or recent rashes.

Social History
He is retired and lives with his wife in a single-story home. He enjoys gardening and walking in the neighborhood. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.

Family History
His father had high blood pressure. His mother had osteoarthritis.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 185 lbs
Height: 5'10"

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Venlafaxine 75 mg daily

Problem List
Status post appendectomy
Status post cholecystectomy
Status post tonsillectomy

Exam
The patient is an alert and oriented 80-year-old male in no acute distress. Physical examination of the lumbar spine reveals mild tenderness to palpation over the L4-L5 region. There is no evidence of spinal deformity or muscle wasting. Straight leg raise tests are negative bilaterally. Gait is steady and balanced.

Assessment
The patient presents with stable chronic low back pain. His symptoms are managed well with conservative measures, and he shows no signs of acute neurological deficit.

Plan
We will continue the current conservative management plan. I advised the patient to continue using heat packs and to practice gentle stretching exercises as previously instructed. We will monitor his progress and schedule a follow-up in three months to assess if any changes in pain intensity are noted.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: An antidepressant on the list does not establish major depression; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
